clue.text: Some of Puzo's sponsors?

definitions.meaning: Mario Puzo's best-known novel is The Godfather, so several of its title figures are in the plural here
those who stand sponsor for a child at its christening

explanation.surface: A question about the backers of a famous novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Christening sponsors are traditionally called godparents, and Puzo's Mafia novel takes its title from the male form.

clue.text: Colourless writer of Westerns

definitions.meaning: Zane ... wrote Riders of the Purple Sage and many other cowboy novels

explanation.surface: A dull author of cowboy stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash-coloured means drab, and Zane Grey was the prolific American author of cowboy novels.

clue.text: All Crimes doe equally the name of Injustice" (Hobbes, Leviathan)

definitions.text: All Crimes doe equally the name of Injustice" (Hobbes, Leviathan)

parts.words: All Crimes doe equally the name of Injustice" (Hobbes, Leviathan)
parts.note: a quotation from Hobbes with one word missing between 'equally' and 'the name': the verb meaning to merit

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has lost its dash: Hobbes wrote that all crimes do equally merit the name of injustice, and the gap takes that verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to merit or be worthy of the name, the sense Hobbes uses in Leviathan.

clue.text: A New Yorkers' playground visualised by

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'A New Yorkers' playground visualised by (1,5,6)', is cut short: the cross-reference (to Ferlinghetti, author of A Coney Island of the Mind) is missing, and no scan or reprint gives it.
annotationWithheld.clue: A New Yorkers' playground visualised by

clue.text: German here at ancient city, extremely gladly finds sacred performance

parts.note: hier is the German word for here
Ur, the ancient Sumerian city, is the crossword's stock ancient city

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extremities of gladly, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A German at an ancient site gladly finds a religious rite.
explanation.definitionFit: Hierurgy is a rare word for a holy rite or liturgical act, a sacred performance.

clue.text: Make more cuts in Henry Reed? It's a shame

indicators.note: in tells us the letters run inside the poet's name and the words after it, ignoring the punctuation

explanation.surface: Should the poet Henry Reed be cut further? A pity if so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' leads into the letters, which run across the question mark; 'a shame' only rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise a film or text again is to cut it once more, an editor's second pass.

clue.text: Like Goldsmith's Tibbs, handsome in Paris

definitions.meaning: ... Tibbs is the shabby would-be dandy in Goldsmith's The Citizen of the World

explanation.surface: Goldsmith's Tibbs compared to a good-looking Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldsmith gave his threadbare dandy the title Beau, and the same word is French for good-looking.

clue.text: American essayist revealed English traits

definitions.meaning: Ralph Waldo ..., the New England essayist
English Traits is ... 1856 book about his visits to Britain

explanation.surface: An American writer exposed the characteristics of the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson is the Concord essayist, and his travel book on Britain is titled English Traits.

clue.text: James memoirs said not to be trustworthy

definitions.meaning: Clive James titled his memoir ... Memoirs, so this is the word said of them

explanation.surface: A writer's memoirs are said to be untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Clive James called his autobiography Unreliable Memoirs, and the adjective means not dependable.

clue.text: Avon's Orient described by Steinbeck?

parts.note: the Orient is the East
Anthony Eden became Earl of Avon, so Avon's means belonging to Eden

explanation.surface: A question about Steinbeck writing of the East near the river Avon.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Eden, the British prime minister, was made Earl of Avon, so 'Avon's' becomes OF EDEN, placed after the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinbeck's 1952 novel is titled after the land where Cain settled in Genesis.

clue.text: Experienced in Vegas by Thompson

parts.note: Hunter S. Thompson's book ... and Loathing in Las Vegas names the two feelings he had there; the first is wanted

explanation.definitionFit: Hunter S. Thompson's gonzo book pairs dread with loathing in Las Vegas, so the first of those is what he felt there.

clue.text: Did he offer Haggard success in possessive form?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Did he offer Haggard success in possessive form? (12)', gives FERLINGHETTI, but no parse of 'offer', 'Haggard' and 'success in possessive form' builds the name's letters; the wordplay cannot be recovered without the setter's key.
annotationWithheld.clue: Did he offer Haggard success in possessive form?

clue.text: Language of obscure seer

indicators.note: obscure here is a verb meaning to blur the word seer into another arrangement

explanation.surface: The tongue of a mysterious prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for Scottish Gaelic, sometimes also Irish Gaelic.

clue.text: Widespread character of Waugh's Baseball Association

definitions.meaning: in Robert Coover's novel The ... Baseball Association, Inc., J. Henry Waugh, Prop., Waugh runs an imaginary league whose name gives this quality

explanation.surface: A general trait of the baseball league run by Waugh.
explanation.walkthrough: Waugh here is not Evelyn but J. Henry Waugh, the accountant in Robert Coover's novel who invents a dice-game league.
explanation.definitionFit: Something general and all-embracing is found everywhere, and Coover's dice-game league is the Universal Baseball Association.

clue.text: Like some of impoverished writer's most welcome accounts

definitions.text: Like some of impoverished writer's most welcome accounts

parts.words: Like some of impoverished writer's most welcome accounts
parts.note: accountants class money owed to a business as accounts of this kind, and a hard-up writer is gladdest of money still to come in

explanation.definitionFit: In bookkeeping, money owed to you sits under accounts of this kind, the ones a poor author longs to collect.

clue.text: Its love described by Dryden

parts.note: Dryden's comedy An ... Love takes its title from a time of day whose love it is

explanation.definitionFit: Dryden's comedy An Evening's Love names the time of day; the plural of that time is the light, ignoring the apostrophe.

clue.text: Composer uses writing material in German city in California

indicators.note: in places the writing material inside the Californian city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
ink is what a pen writes with

explanation.surface: A composer writes with ink in a German city in California.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Glinka was the Russian composer of A Life for the Tsar.

clue.text: "Speak her fair and canny, or we will have a — hasp on the yarn-windles " (Scott, The Pirate)

definitions.text: "Speak her fair and canny, or we will have a — hasp on the yarn-windles " (Scott, The Pirate)

parts.words: "Speak her fair and canny, or we will have a — hasp on the yarn-windles " (Scott, The Pirate)
parts.note: a quotation from Scott's The Pirate with the adjective before hasp left out; a tangled skein on the winding reel

explanation.definitionFit: A hasp of yarn that is tangled or snarled is in a knot; Scott's word for that state fills the gap.

clue.text: Take shape in measures for philosopher

indicators.note: in places the setting jelly inside the printers' measures

parts.note: ens are printers' measures of width
to gel is to set or take shape

explanation.surface: Something firming up among measurements, for a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's unit of width, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels was the German philosopher who co-wrote The Communist Manifesto.

clue.text: "Safe haven" (with gin cocktail) for Cornish novelist

parts.note: gold is the classic safe-haven investment in uncertain markets

indicators.note: cocktail means a mixed drink, so the letters of gin are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Cornish writer's refuge, with a gin cocktail to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes GIN into ING; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: William Golding, author of Lord of the Flies, was born in Cornwall.

clue.text: General subject of Harris?

definitions.meaning: the Carthaginian commander who crossed the Alps
Thomas Harris wrote novels about the cannibal Dr Lecter, one titled with his first name

explanation.surface: A military leader written about by Harris.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannibal was the Carthaginian commander, and Hannibal Lecter is the subject of Thomas Harris's thrillers.

clue.text: Smollett lieutenant apparently in the field

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Smollett lieutenant apparently in the field (7)', gives Lieutenant Bowling and the cricket sense of bowling, but no word defines BAWLING (crying); a definition appears to be missing from the held text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Smollett lieutenant apparently in the field

clue.text: Old lawyer exposes nearly two hundred before hesitation over nothing

parts.note: CIC is the Roman numeral 199, one short of two hundred
er is the sound of a pause
O is the figure zero

explanation.surface: An ancient lawyer lays bare nearly two hundred before pausing over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: CIC is 199 in Roman numerals (one before two hundred); 'before' and 'over' just order the pieces down the grid, and 'exposes' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Tullius Cicero was the great orator and advocate of the Roman Republic.

clue.text: Tender message from Baronne Dudevant?

definitions.meaning: a love note sent on 14 February
the Baronne Dudevant wrote as George Sand, and one of her novels has this title

explanation.surface: A love note from a French baroness.
explanation.definitionFit: A loving card sent on St Valentine's Day carries the saint's name, and George Sand's 1832 novel is called Valentine.

clue.text: That of Ted Hughes observed in inclement weather

definitions.text: That of Ted Hughes observed in inclement weather

parts.words: That of Ted Hughes observed in inclement weather
parts.note: Ted Hughes's first collection was The ___ in the Rain, a bird of prey seen in wet weather

explanation.definitionFit: Hughes's debut collection The Hawk in the Rain shows the bird of prey hovering in bad weather.

clue.text: One begotten by Wells top of the bill

definitions.meaning: H. G. Wells wrote the novel ... Begotten

explanation.definitionFit: Wells's late novel is Star Begotten, and the headline performer is the celebrity heading the bill.

clue.text: Leaders of book readers in Oldham show spirit

indicators.note: the leaders of the four words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Bookish readers in the Lancashire town of Oldham show some verve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' only joins the letters to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or verve, a borrowing from Italian.

clue.text: Little Serb turns out to be writer of aesthetic essays

indicators.note: turns out signals the letters of the phrase are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A small Serbian proves to be an essayist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' only links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A belletrist writes literary pieces valued for style and beauty rather than information.

clue.text: Spender's limit (of existence)

parts.note: Stephen Spender's novel The ___ of Being names the boundary of existence

explanation.definitionFit: Spender's novel The Edge of Being takes this word for the brink or boundary of existence.

clue.text: With which Fleming displayed the Midas touch?

definitions.text: With which Fleming displayed the Midas touch?

parts.words: With which Fleming displayed the Midas touch?
parts.note: Midas turned everything he touched to gold, and Ian Fleming named a Bond villain after a digit of that metal

explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming's Bond novel is named for a gold-obsessed villain, the Midas touch being a hand that turns things to gold.
